facts.raw_span: slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles
Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Negative for: synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography revealed no evidence of primary or secondary tumors

concepts.why: The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, tumor cells dispersed in an 'Indian file pattern', and positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies support the diagnosis of apocrine gland carcinoma.

The presence of a solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla and positive immunohistochemistry for cytokeratin 20 and GATA3 antibodies support the diagnosis of extramammary Paget disease.

The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, tumor cells dispersed in an 'Indian file pattern', and positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin and cytokeratin 20 support the diagnosis of hidradenocarcinoma.

The presence of isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells in a sentinel lymph node and the lack of evidence of primary or secondary tumors on imaging studies support the diagnosis of metastatic breast carcinoma.
The presence of a solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla and multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands support the diagnosis of apocrine adenoma.
The presence of a solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla and dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat support the diagnosis of hidradenoma.
The presence of progressive infiltration of the overlying skin and mild episodic pain in the right axilla during menstrual cycles support the diagnosis of inflammatory carcinoma of the breast.
The presence of a solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla and dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat support the diagnosis of dermatofibroma.

rationales.F01: Subcutaneous node growth is non-specific and can be seen in various conditions.
rationales.F02: Progressive skin infiltration suggests an aggressive tumor, which is more typical of carcinomas than benign conditions.
rationales.F06: Dermal tumor infiltration without epidermal involvement is characteristic of certain carcinomas, including apocrine gland carcinoma.
rationales.F07: The 'Indian file pattern' is a distinctive histological feature of some carcinomas, including apocrine gland carcinoma.
rationales.F08: Positive immunohistochemistry for specific markers, such as GATA3 and estrogen receptor, supports the diagnosis of apocrine gland carcinoma.
rationales.F10: The presence of GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association with tumor cells is highly suggestive of apocrine gland carcinoma.
rationales.F11: The presence of cytokeratin-positive tumor cells in a sentinel lymph node indicates lymph node involvement, which is more typical of malignant conditions.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration, along with the 'Indian file pattern' of tumor cells, supports apocrine gland carcinoma as the most likely diagnosis.
